description: Protected visual oracle and hard cutover gates for the browserless native WFDiag Windows Reactor migration.

baseline.capture_status: all 18 dark-theme states captured from Store-signed 2.5.8 and paired at matching viewports with the final native ARM64 candidate; variant and acceptance review remains pending

visual_acceptance_categories.acceptance: The same primary destinations, commands, overlays, hierarchy, and cross-screen transitions remain discoverable in the same context.
Labels, values, status semantics, empty/loading/error states, destructive confirmations, and streamed output preserve current behavior and meaning.
Protected logos, wallpapers, avatar, semantic colors, rounded-card hierarchy, and translucent visual character are retained using native WinUI materials.
Default, minimum, desktop, and compact widths preserve reading order, visual hierarchy, usable density, and scroll behavior without clipping.
Type hierarchy and icon meaning match the existing interface; native WinUI metrics and Fluent symbols are accepted where they improve platform fidelity.
Progress, streaming, navigation, hover/press, success/error, and cancellation feedback remain timely and respect reduced-motion settings.
Keyboard order and shortcuts, focus restoration, automation names/roles, Narrator announcements, text scaling, and high contrast pass native Windows testing.
Charts, scan rings, sparklines, tables, and status colors preserve the same data, scale, labels, and non-color text alternatives.

backend_parity.summary: A UI-neutral nonblocking native worker owns the canonical architecture, Windows version, machine-name, and elevation contracts shared with Tauri. Reactor now starts that worker off the UI thread, renders the live host/OS/elevation result, exposes native/emulated architecture in the machine-card automation name, rejects stale completions, and blocks scan selection until elevation is known. A fixture-free native ARM64 run matched the Store 2.5.8 Diagnostics viewport at 1440x1000 logical / 2160x1500 physical, loaded local XAML, loaded no WebView module, closed gracefully, and produced no crash event. Elevated, error, emulated, x64, and full accessibility matrices remain open.

Quick and Full scans execute through the UI-neutral native runtime with progress, task-granular cancellation, stale-session protection, selectable result details, Settings-backed custom Quick Scan tasks, authoritative post-scan issue projection, optional Store-compatible history auto-save, and native export/share entry points. Full admin/non-admin, cancellation-race, collector-error, x64/ARM64, accessibility, and long-run interaction matrices remain unfinished, so status stays partial.

The canonical issue catalog and deterministic detectors run through a UI-neutral nonblocking worker shared with Tauri. Reactor commits each complete authoritative native result map before optional history persistence, prepares detection evidence off the UI thread, rejects stale request/session/epoch completions, renders returned issues plus maintenance actions, and reruns detection after remediation. Live populated/empty/error/remediation-refresh, x64/ARM64, and accessibility matrices remain open, so status stays partial.

Tiered remediation execution and elevation relaunch use the shared engine. Maintenance, per-issue Run, and AI stage_remediation requests all enter the Reactor action broker as opaque expiring one-use proposals; approval revalidates current scan/issue/catalog fingerprints, and Repair requires a second explicit confirmation plus the engine tier gate. Interactive Run/proposal/expiry/revalidation/Repair capture remains open, so status stays partial.

Live system samples flow directly into Reactor through a bounded native event bus. Revisioned window visibility, focus, and minimize snapshots now pause the monitor while the window is unusable, cancel pending process work, and resume with a refresh only when lifecycle state owned the pause. Long-run lease behavior, failure recovery, x64/accessibility evidence, and the network-connections view still need parity validation.

The live Reactor screen queries the native monitor worker off the UI thread and renders real filtered, sortable, selectable, paged and virtualized process rows with stale-request protection. ARM64 expanded-desktop load, pause/resume, refresh, filter, sort, details, scroll, page 2, full-width row alignment, native-XAML module, zero-WebView, and zero-WER validation pass; compact/collapsed, x64 runtime, accessibility, and long-run soak coverage remain open.

Reactor owns the UI-neutral history worker, reads the existing Store-compatible DPAPI v2 scan store off the UI thread, and renders live tag-aware filtering and label fallback, selection, refresh, independently editable labels and tags, failure trends, and destructive clear behind explicit confirmation. Comparison summaries render regressed, recovered, and output-changed rows; expanding one lazily requests only that task's stored outputs, rejects stale completions, and shows explicit loading/error state plus side-by-side previous/current text. Selecting the latest scan invalidates stale comparisons and identifies it as the baseline, while a refreshed list recomputes an existing comparison when its newest baseline changes. Completed scans auto-save from the authoritative diagnostic session snapshot after the Store-matching cancellable 500 ms window, with explicit history-contract conversion and live retention/catalog providers; auto-save-off sends no request, retention-off acknowledges without persistence, failures are nonfatal, and deterministic captures touch no storage. The remaining live loading/error/x64/ARM64/accessibility interaction matrices remain unfinished, so status stays partial.

The shared UI-neutral worker generates the shipping JSON, text, HTML, WindowsForum, clipboard, and email payloads, plus a recipient-free percent-encoded email-draft URI that never contains the full diagnostic report. Reactor wires owner-validated native save picking, format/extension enforcement, background rendering and file writes, silent picker cancellation, typed picker/path failures surfaced with their detail in the native status UI, WindowsForum post copy to the Windows clipboard through the WinRT DataTransfer API, and the allowlisted new-thread launch. The visible Email Report command queues the shared email renderer; successful completion copies the full report body to the Windows clipboard and calls a typed Windows launcher that can open only the recipient-free unsent draft, while render, clipboard, and launch failures remain user-visible. The full picker-cancel/picker-error/write-failure/clipboard/browser/mail-client/x64/ARM64/accessibility interaction matrices remain open, so status stays partial.

Reactor owns the canonical settings worker and Store-compatible JSON/DPAPI persistence service. The native dialog loads persisted values off the UI thread, edits every visible non-secret 2.5.8 field plus provider endpoint/model setup and custom Quick Scan tasks, manages per-provider credentials through typed secret operations, previews theme changes, restores the persisted snapshot on Cancel, commits only a matching successful Save response, and rejects stale completions. A cancellable off-UI model-catalog worker resolves from the current draft endpoint, CLI path, and credential state; the dialog renders Refresh/Cancel, selectable results, blocked/loading/error state, and stale-last-successful-list fallback while retaining manual entry. Typed Codex/Claude account workers and component handlers drive Check, Sign in, Sign out, and Cancel controls with operation status, detail, and errors; status checks also participate in catalog refresh. The shipping one-click CLI installer remains outside Reactor until its winget/vendor bootstrap has a confirmed process-tree cancellation boundary; users currently install the official CLI themselves. Saved close-to-tray state updates the live window hook and saved notification state gates scan-completion toasts. Persisted scan-on-startup arms a one-use state gate, waits until settings plus system-info and architecture initialization are terminal, consumes before starting exactly one Quick Scan, and is always suppressed in deterministic visual mode. ARM64 self-contained automation passed cancel/reopen and save/restart persistence without changing the host Store settings file, loading WebView, or producing WER/Application Error evidence. Live startup-scan and provider-specific catalog/CLI/browser/account/installer evidence, side-effect interaction tests, x64 runtime, accessibility, and the complete validation/error matrix remain unfinished, so status stays partial.

The Tauri-free ProviderManagementService composes the exact provider/preference/status contracts, capabilities and routing policy, Store-identity validation, shared response cache, shipping probes, and typed worker used by Tauri. Reactor instantiates it with the shared settings adapter and concrete Phi, Foundry Local, Ollama, custom-endpoint, and Codex/Claude CLI sources and renders the resolved live provider state. Its Settings flow now drives cancellable live model catalogs from draft configuration, presents selectable results with blocked/loading/error/stale states, and keeps manual model entry available. A separate typed Codex/Claude account worker and component handlers drive Check, Sign in, Sign out, and Cancel controls with operation status, detail, and errors. Automated CLI installation remains open pending a confirmed process-tree cancellation boundary. Auto-selected local-provider clean failures honor persisted Ask/Allow/Never cloud consent; explicit provider selections never fall back, and an allowed local-to-cloud transition is disclosed with ProviderUse fallback attribution. The status remains partial pending provider-specific live catalog/account/CLI/browser/installer/loading/error/fallback matrices, accessibility, and packaged Phi/Aion evidence.

The native chat worker starts by default and resolves every turn from live DPAPI-backed settings. OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and DeepSeek APIs; Foundry Local, Ollama, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints; signed-in Codex and Claude Code subscriptions; and package-bound Phi route through shared transports. Streaming, immediate in-flight cancellation, backend-owned conversation/New Conversation, stale-request rejection, exactly-one terminal projection, and the canonical exact-ten bounded tool catalog are wired. Auto-selected local-provider clean failures honor persisted Ask/Allow/Never cloud consent; explicit providers never fall back, and allowed local-to-cloud transitions are disclosed with ProviderUse fallback attribution. The closed parser admits only run_diagnostic, search_windows_knowledge, get_scan_summary, request_full_scan, get_detected_issues, compare_with_previous_scan, get_live_stats, list_remediations, list_scan_history, and stage_remediation with bounded closed arguments; scan/remediation calls create typed consent/proposal events and never execute directly. Ask AI immediately sends structured current-issue evidence. Prioritize / Propose fix plan uses a cancellable native worker with the shared bounded catalog-ID prompt/parser, stale fingerprint rejection, provider attribution, local-only Auto retry, and the normal tiered action broker for every selected action. Mandatory hermetic engine/UIA gates cover custom-provider chat, cancel, exact tool names, and a real remediation-catalog round trip. Provider-specific live Windows and fallback success/error/accessibility evidence, packaged Phi, live issue-to-chat/fix-plan evidence, and the remaining error matrices stay open, so status remains partial.

The native report worker starts by default and routes the same API, local, subscription, and Phi provider set through the shared ReportService. Streaming, duplicate suppression, immediate cancellation, exactly-one terminal projection, provider attribution, force-refresh Regenerate, shared-fingerprint cache identity, and full cached-body rehydration are wired. Reactor resolves the newest different stored scan off-thread for changed-since-last-scan evidence; compact evidence and Auto Phi-to-next-local reroute policies are shared and tested. The mandatory hermetic UIA gate asserts streamed report content and a fresh deterministic regeneration; shared service/worker tests separately pin cache and cached-body paths. Provider-specific and packaged live Windows evidence plus error and accessibility matrices remain open, so status stays partial.

Reactor chat/report now route Phi through the shared package-bound Windows adapter, and provider status uses the shared identity-gated Phi probe. The gate remains blocked because Phi/Aion activation, Store identity/capability readback, runtime alignment, model readiness, fallback behavior, and real Copilot+ x64/ARM64 execution have not been validated through a Reactor package.

restart-as-administrator (runas relaunch) and allowlisted external links implemented through shared launchers; live candidate exercised process startup and graceful close without elevation prompts. Interactive UAC capture still open.

Native save picking, Windows clipboard delivery through the WinRT DataTransfer API, allowlisted browser launch, and the AUMID-bound scan-completion toast are implemented. Save-dialog cancellation is a silent no-op; actual picker/path failures remain typed and surface with detail in the native status UI. The live candidate invokes the toast after completed scan finalization when notifications are enabled; failures are best-effort and do not affect scan completion. Interactive picker cancellation/error capture, clipboard/browser delivery, packaged-toast capture, and x64/ARM64/accessibility matrices remain open.

Reactor now owns the UI-neutral update worker plus the Store 2.5.8 five-second startup delay, once-per-24-hour fail-open throttle, five-second informational notice with exact hover pause/resume, native About dialog, stale-dialog protection, and an explicit typed action boundary that accepts only the exact WFDiag GitHub release tag for the returned semantic version. Throttle path/read work runs off the UI thread and timer completions are epoch- and generation-scoped. Store/debug/no-update/network/runtime failures remain silent and deterministic capture modes perform no update I/O. Packaged Store/direct x64 and ARM64 runtime, persistence, accessibility, and browser-launch validation remain open.

Tray icon, close-to-tray, Show/Hide/Quick Scan/Exit, hidden/minimized restore, and forced exit run through the isolated comctl32 subclass and Shell_NotifyIconW. The exact Reactor HWND is registered independently of visibility and cleared with stale-window protection; coherent revisioned visible/minimized/focused/tray snapshots are polled by the component and drive monitor pause/resume. The subclass was active during the live ARM64 validation run, which closed gracefully. Menu, close-to-tray, minimize/focus, restoration, and accessibility interaction capture remain open, so status stays partial.

The single-instance mutex decided primary/secondary at startup during every live run. Second-launch handoff uses the activation event and the exact registered main-window HWND, which remains available while hidden; minimized windows restore, hidden windows show, and foreground activation is best-effort under Windows policy. The interactive hidden/minimized second-launch focus matrix remains open, so status stays partial.

Native command palette (filtered command list, titlebar entry) and shortcut help dialog parity; expressible accelerators are wired (Ctrl+R refresh, Ctrl+Numpad1..6 screens). The full shipping set (Ctrl+1..6 main row, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+Shift+Q/F) is not expressible in the pinned AcceleratorKey enum (Control-only modifiers; numpad digits, R, Enter, arithmetic keys only) — upstream gap.

upstream_api_gates.summary: Owner decision 2026-09-01: the isolated Win32 interop in apps/wfdiag/src/window_support.rs and instance_support.rs (cached exact HWND, revisioned lifecycle snapshots, close-to-tray, show/hide/minimize/restore, tray menu) is the accepted implementation for this release; an official Reactor window-lifecycle API remains a tracked follow-up.

Owner decision 2026-09-01: Ctrl+K, Ctrl+1..6, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+Shift+Q and Ctrl+Shift+F are delivered by the isolated Win32 keyboard hook in apps/wfdiag/src/window_support.rs with pure policy tests; Ctrl+R and Ctrl+Numpad1..6 use Reactor accelerators. Accepted for this release; an official Reactor accelerator API that can express the full chord set remains a tracked follow-up.

cutover_gates.summary: Owner decision 2026-09-01: ship on the reviewed windows-rs revision 1be5649497b59fe7cc2fb0ae5b0ebd7787327cc8 (Reactor 0.100.0 source). crates.io still publishes only the placeholder 0.0.0 for windows-reactor and windows-reactor-setup (re-checked 2026-09-01); the pin is exact (revision, not branch), reviewed, and recorded in the root Cargo.lock. Migrating to an official release is a follow-up, not a cutover blocker.

All 18 core dark-theme baseline states are captured from the installed Microsoft Store WFDiag 2.5.8 build. The gate remains blocked until light, high-contrast, DPI, and reduced-motion variants are captured and the complete reference set receives parity review.
All six screens and their interaction states have not yet passed parity review using Reactor-owned native WinUI controls only; WebView2 and browser-hosted UI are prohibited.
Aion/Phi behavior has not passed on real Copilot+ x64 and ARM64 devices with the preserved Store identity and Reactor runtime strategy.
The Reactor x64/ARM64 MSIX bundle has not passed clean-machine install, identity/capability readback, signing, and Store certification validation.
Signed self-contained x64/ARM64 MSI, NSIS, and portable-directory distributions have not passed clean-machine install and uninstall tests.
